Case: Reset form is displayed with pre-filled email when Forgot your password link is clicked
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the login password step and has entered an identifier (email or username).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-009 · AC1
  • AC Quote: "Forgot your password?" link on login password step opens reset form with one field labelled "EMAIL", pre-filled with the identifier; "Send link" and "Back" buttons.
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the SleekFlow login page.
  2. Enter a valid email or username on the identifier step and proceed to the password step.
  3. Click the "Forgot your password?" link.
  4. Observe the reset password form.
Expected:
• Reset password form is displayed.
  • A single field labelled "EMAIL" is present and pre-filled with the identifier entered on the login step.
  • "Send link" and "Back" buttons are both visible.
BDD: Given the user is on the login password step with a valid identifier, When the user clicks "Forgot your password?", Then the reset form opens with the EMAIL field pre-filled and both Send link and Back buttons visible.

Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the password reset form (reached via "Forgot your password?" on the login password step).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-009 · AC1
  • AC Quote: "Forgot your password?" link on login password step opens reset form … "Send link" and "Back" buttons.
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the password reset form via the login flow.
  2. Click the "Back" button on the reset form.
  3. Observe the resulting page.
Expected:

  • No data loss on the identifier field.
BDD: Given the user is on the password reset form, When the user clicks Back, Then the login password step is displayed again.

Case: No email or username appears in any URL during the password-reset flow
Description:
• Pre-condition: User initiates the password reset flow with a known email address. NOTE: This test is blocked pending the Auth0 spike (TBD — Auth0 may not support removing email from URL).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-009 · AC3
  • AC Quote: No URL in the flow contains the email or username. Currently the password-reset link puts the user's email address in the URL (logged and cached — personal data exposure).
Test Steps:
1. Open browser developer tools and monitor the address bar and network requests.
  2. Navigate to the login page and enter a known email address (e.g. testuser@example.com).
  3. Proceed to the password step and click "Forgot your password?".
  4. Inspect the URL at every step of the reset flow (reset form, check-your-email page, any redirect).
  5. Also inspect network request URLs for any occurrence of the email value.
Expected:
• No URL in the entire reset flow contains the user's email address or username in any form (plain text, encoded, or hashed).
  • Browser address bar does not expose PII at any step.
BDD: Given a user initiates password reset with a known email, When every URL in the reset flow is inspected, Then no URL contains the email or username in any form.

Case: Inline error is shown and no request is sent when a non-email value is submitted on the reset form
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the password reset form.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-009 · AC4
  • AC Quote: Given "not an email" or a value with spaces, when Send link is clicked, then an inline error shows and no request is sent.
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the password reset form.
  2. Clear the EMAIL field and type "not an email" (a plain string with no @ symbol).
  3. Click "Send link".
  4. Observe the form and monitor network requests (browser DevTools Network tab).
Expected:
• An inline error message is displayed beneath or adjacent to the EMAIL field.
  • No HTTP request is sent to the password-reset endpoint.
  • The user remains on the reset form.
  • The error message contains no empty placeholders (e.g. no "between and characters").
BDD: Given the reset form is displayed, When the user submits "not an email" as the input, Then an inline error is shown and no network request is made.

Case: Error message contains no empty placeholders when invalid input is submitted on the reset form
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the password reset form with the current broken validation message in scope: "Username can only contain alphanumeric characters or: ''. Username should have between and characters."
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-009 · AC5
  • AC Quote: Current broken pattern message shows: "Username can only contain alphanumeric characters or: ''. Username should have between and characters." (empty placeholders). This must be fixed.
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the password reset form.
  2. Enter an invalid value that previously triggered the broken pattern message (e.g. a username-style string with special characters).
  3. Click "Send link".
  4. Read the displayed error message carefully.
Expected:
• The error message is fully rendered with no empty placeholder gaps (no occurrences of "between and characters" with missing values).
  • All numeric values in the message are populated (e.g. "between 3 and 20 characters").
BDD: Given the reset form with an invalid input that triggers a pattern validation, When the user clicks Send link, Then the error message contains no empty placeholder values.

Case: Check Your Email page is shown after a valid-format email is submitted on the reset form
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the password reset form; AC4 validation is in place (valid email format is required).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-009 · AC2
  • AC Quote: Any value, including "not an email", lands on "Check Your Email" with "Resend email" — no enumeration, no validation (current state; AC4 changes this to require valid format).
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the password reset form.
  2. Enter a properly formatted email address (e.g. testuser@example.com).
  3. Click "Send link".
  4. Observe the resulting page.
Expected:
• "Check Your Email" page is displayed.
  • "Resend email" button or link is present on the page.
  • No indication of whether the email address exists in the system (no account enumeration).
BDD: Given the reset form with a valid email address entered, When the user clicks Send link, Then the Check Your Email page is displayed with a Resend email option.

Case: Resend email link is present and functional on the Check Your Email page
Description:
• Pre-condition: User has successfully submitted a valid email on the reset form and reached the Check Your Email page.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-009 · AC2
  • AC Quote: Any value … lands on "Check Your Email" with "Resend email".
Test Steps:
1. Complete the password reset submission with a valid email address to reach the Check Your Email page.
  2. Locate the "Resend email" element.
  3. Click "Resend email".
  4. Observe the page response.
Expected:
• "Resend email" button or link is visible on the Check Your Email page.
  • Clicking it triggers a confirmation or feedback (e.g. brief disabled state, success message, or same page refresh) without navigating away unexpectedly.
BDD: Given the user is on the Check Your Email page, When the user clicks Resend email, Then the action is acknowledged and no error is shown.

Case: Password reset confirmation message contains the submitted email value when shown
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the password reset form; feature uses the confirmation message pattern from Appendix B.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-009 · AC2, AC5
  • AC Quote: Appendix B confirmation: "Please check the email address associated with the username {value} for instructions to reset your password." No message ever shows empty placeholders.
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the password reset form.
  2. Enter a valid email address (e.g. testuser@example.com).
  3. Click "Send link".
  4. Read the confirmation or Check Your Email page content.
Expected:
• If a confirmation message referencing the submitted value is displayed, the placeholder {value} is replaced with the actual email address entered by the user.
  • No literal brace-enclosed placeholder (e.g. {value}) is visible on screen.
BDD: Given a valid email is submitted on the reset form, When the confirmation message is displayed, Then the message shows the actual email value with no unreplaced placeholders.
